# Probe — measure what would change the decision

Identify the smallest claim that can change the next action. First inspect available
evidence, its exact inputs, method, version and original decision criteria. Reuse what
already answers the question; label absent provenance and retrospective criteria.

For new measurements, state the result-to-decision rule before running. Compare
equivalent inputs and vary the disputed factor. Control timing boundaries, output
format, cold/warm caches, order and competing resource use when measuring speed.
Distinguish correctness, perceptual quality, speed and workflow benefit.

Size the trial to the unresolved decision. Use representative inputs and a falsifiable
reference. A null result or conflicting evidence is a result. Limit conclusions to
the tested conditions; do not promote a tone's frequency or a few spot checks into
whole-signal or whole-workflow equivalence.

State model, trial scale and paid scope before a live-provider experiment, reuse
existing authority and stay within it. Fixtures can isolate a mechanism but must be
identified as fixtures. Keep product code outside an experiment-only request.

Report the method, observations, verdict and limits. For a design-only request, stop
at the proposed experiment. Keep scratch disposable and use `references/saving.md`
only for a requested or independently reusable retained result.
